title: Kirby Corporation (US-KEX) - LIVE deep dive #2, first US live run (random draw from an SEC frame, protocol v1.3 stages 2-7): method test, no verdict; card size 0; 6 live calls
body: LIVE method test (L9, L21): company drawn at random from an SEC-built frame; no buy/sell verdict. Research, not advice. SELECTION: 8 dei:EntityPublicFloat frames -> 2,161 candidates -> 1,037 in frame (float $500M-$10B on the latest 10-K; financials/REITs/SPACs/utilities/no-revenue biotech removed) -> sorted by CIK, random.Random(20261124).shuffle; KEX drawn first and passed all checks (no merger, no 4.01/4.02 in 3 yrs - one 4.02 in Jul-2020, ICFR effective, solvency S1/S5 0, SUE CY2026Q3 +2.58 quintile 5). KEY FINDINGS: (1) Kirby earns about its cost of capital (proxy ROTC 10.4% 2023-25) even near the top of the inland cycle (utilization low-90%, industry newbuilds 60-70/yr just replace retirements); (2) contract escalators decelerated (+9.5% Jan-2024 -> +3-5% Jan-2025), term share rose 60->65->70%; (3) 2026 is a fuel-shock year ($3.91/gal Q3 vs $2.46) after the Iran conflict, with a ~120-day escalator lag, plus a federal Jones Act waiver (17-Mar-2026, extended to 14-Feb-2027); (4) KDS pivoted to data-center power (power gen ~46-52% of KDS, backlog > $1.5bn; new 10-K risk factor); (5) receivables +36% YoY vs revenue +12%; 21 insider sales, 0 buys. VALUATION: $122.89 = 19.4x FY25 EPS, 17.0x FY26 guide, 9.5x EV/EBITDA, FCF yield 6.3%. Worksheet (ROIIC 10%, pre-registered) DCF $58.6 (prob-weighted), EV 5-yr multiple 1.12x vs hurdle 1.47x -> card size 0; a post-output ROIIC 20% sensitivity still gives EV 1.17x. Method finding: the NOPAT-based worksheet ignores cash-tax deferral from bonus depreciation (FY25 FCF 406 > NOPAT 374), so it under-values capex-heavy US firms; on reported FCF the price implies ~3.8% perpetual growth (roughly fair). Promise ledger (6 calls, Q2-25..Q3-26): 79% credit (n=12) vs US-industrials peer median 84%. Calls: FY26 EPS >= 7.28 (P 0.35 vs 0.50), revenue growth >= 9% (0.62 vs 0.40), op margin >= 14% (0.55 vs 0.50), capex in $220-260M (0.82 vs 0.60), Jones Act waiver extended past 14-Feb-2027 (0.55 vs 0.50), beats SPY to 30-Sep-2027 (0.42 vs 0.45); card 5-yr calls P(>=3x) 0.004, P(<=0.5x) 0.04, blow-up 0.02 (EST bases 0.10/0.12/0.04).

title: Kirby (US-KEX) variant view, Nov 2026: no claimable mispricing; mild negative tilt (return on capital ~ cost of capital at a cyclical high)
body: Market appears to price an inland up-cycle plus a data-center power-gen growth story at 17x forward EPS / 9.5x EV/EBITDA. Our view: no claimable mispricing; on reported FCF the price is roughly fair (~3.8% perpetual growth at 9.5% CoE), on NOPAT with honest reinvestment it is rich. Evidence: ROTC 10.4% (2023-25), escalators decelerating, term renewals flat-to-low-single-digit 2025-26, fuel lag, Jones Act waiver, receivables build, insider selling. Proves us wrong: FY26 EPS >= 7.28, 2027 renewals high-single digits, power-gen growth > 20%. Scored by thesis:paper-call:US-KEX:*.

title: Paper call: Kirby FY2026 diluted EPS is >= $7.28 (top of the 10-15% growth guide)
body: Deep-dive-generated forward test (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Live deep dive #2 (first US live run), company drawn at random (method test, L9/L21). Probability 0.35 (naive base rate 0.50) that: Kirby FY2026 diluted EPS is >= $7.28 (top of the 10-15% growth guide). Our reasoning: 9M-2026 EPS $5.26, so Q4 needs >= $2.02 (+20% YoY vs $1.68); Q3-26 was $2.09 but Q4 carries winter weather, heavy coastal shipyards and fuel still ~$3.9/gal with a ~120-day escalator lag; management's 'toward the upper end' implies ~$7.20-7.25; buybacks cut the share count ~5% YoY. Naive base: management guided 'upper end of 10-15%'; hitting or beating the exact top of a narrowed range is treated as a coin flip (Kirby's one prior full-year guide, 2025's 15-25%, was delivered at the low end: +16%). Resolution: YES if diluted EPS for fiscal 2026 (year to 31-Dec-2026), as first reported in the FY2026 10-K XBRL (EarningsPerShareDiluted), is >= 7.28. Source: SEC XBRL companyfacts (10-K FY2026). Resolve by 2027-03-31; score with Brier vs the base rate to test whether deep-dive probabilities beat naive base rates.

title: Paper call: Kirby FY2026 revenue grows >= 9.0% (>= ~$3,667M vs $3,364.1M)

Probability 0.62 (naive base rate 0.40) that: Kirby FY2026 revenue grows >= 9.0% (>= ~$3,667M vs $3,364.1M). Our reasoning: 9M-2026 revenue +9.2%; Q4 needs >= $923M (+8.4% vs $851.8M). title: Paper call: Kirby FY2026 GAAP operating margin is >= 14.0%
body: Deep-dive-generated forward test (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Live deep dive #2 (first US live run), company drawn at random (method test, L9/L21). Probability 0.55 (naive base rate 0.50) that: Kirby FY2026 GAAP operating margin is >= 14.0%. Our reasoning: 9M-2026 operating margin 13.9% (380.9/2,743.7); FY >= 14.0% needs a Q4 margin of ~14.3% on ~$935M revenue. title: Paper call: The federal Jones Act waiver (first issued 17-Mar-2026) is extended again, or replaced, so that it is in effect after 14-Feb-2027
body: Deep-dive-generated forward test (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Live deep dive #2 (first US live run), company drawn at random (method test, L9/L21). Probability 0.55 (naive base rate 0.50) that: The federal Jones Act waiver (first issued 17-Mar-2026) is extended again, or replaced, so that it is in effect after 14-Feb-2027. Our reasoning: Already extended three times (to mid-May, mid-Aug, mid-Nov 2026, then to 14-Feb-2027) while fuel stayed elevated after the Iran conflict; opposition from maritime groups and Jones Act supporters in Congress is rising and fuel has eased from the Q2-26 peak ($4.23/gal to $3.91 in Q3). Naive base: coin flip on a renewal decision with a three-for-three history but growing political resistance. Resolution: YES if DHS/CBP extend the waiver or issue a successor covering petroleum products with an expiry after 14-Feb-2027, announced by 28-Feb-2027; a lapse on 14-Feb-2027 = NO. Kirby's FY2026 10-K risk factor is the filing cross-check. Source: DHS/CBP notices; KEX FY2026 10-K Item 1A (EDGAR). Resolve by 2027-03-15; score with Brier vs the base rate to test whether deep-dive probabilities beat naive base rates.

Probability 0.42 (naive base rate 0.45) that: KEX total price return from 20-Nov-2026 (close $122.89) to 30-Sep-2027 beats SPY (close $689.81 on 20-Nov-2026). Our reasoning: no edge on the cycle claimed; the worksheet DCF sits well below the price and insiders sold $22M with no buys, against ~4-5%/yr buybacks, a strong 2026 print (EPS +14%) and a power-gen backlog; the stock fell 16% from $146 (28-Oct) into a falling market, so part of the de-rating has happened. title: Decision card US-KEX 2026-11-23 (paper)
body: Decision card v1 for Kirby Corporation. Rule output: size 0: blocked by Expected value vs hurdle (EV 1.12x vs hurdle 1.47x → below hurdle → size 0). Thesis: Method-test thesis: Kirby is a cyclical, capital-heavy tank-barge operator (28% of the ~4,004-barge US inland fleet, Jones Act protected) plus an engine/power-generation distributor riding data-center backup and prime-power demand; over 5 years it compounds EPS ~4-9%/yr (pricing on a near-fixed fleet plus ~4-5%/yr buybacks) at a return on total capital close to its cost of capital (~10%), so shareholder returns track EPS plus buybacks minus any de-rating from today's ~17x forward P/E. Variant view: Market (reverse DCF): at $122.89 (19.4x FY25 EPS, 17.0x the FY26 guide, 9.5x EV/EBITDA, FCF yield 6.3%) the worksheet's NOPAT-based DCF cannot reproduce the price at a 10% ROIIC; even at a 20% ROIIC (sensitivity file, written after the outputs) the price needs ~11%/yr revenue growth for 10 years or a 17% NOPAT margin (FY25 11.1%). On reported FCF the price is consistent with ~3.8% perpetual FCF growth at a 9.5% cost of equity, i.e. roughly fair if 2025's cash taxes (bonus depreciation, deferred tax $82M) persist. Our view: NO claimable mispricing, with a mild negative tilt. What the market appears to price: an inland up-cycle (utilization low-90%, term renewals 'north of inflation', newbuilds 60-70/yr only matching retirements) plus a power-generation growth story (backlog > $1.5bn, book-to-bill > 1). What we verified that cuts against it: (1) ROTC 10.4% over 2023-25 (proxy) - the business earns about its cost of capital even at good points of the cycle; (2) contract escalators slowed from +9.5% (Jan-2024) to +3-5% (Jan-2025) and term renewals were flat to low-single-digit in 2025-26 - the rate cycle has been decelerating, not accelerating; (3) 2026 inland margins are capped by fuel ($3.91/gal Q3-26 vs $2.46) with a ~120-day escalator lag, and the Jones Act waiver (17-Mar-2026, now extended to 14-Feb-2027) adds foreign-flag competition risk in coastal; (4) 21 open-market insider sales, 0 buys in 12 months (weak signal, L14); (5) receivables +36% YoY vs revenue +12% (fuel-related, but CFO 9M-26 $313M vs $358M). What would prove us wrong: FY2026 EPS above the top of the guide (>= $7.28) with 2027 term renewals up high-single digits and power-gen revenue growth > 20% - i.e. a genuine margin step-up, not a buyback-driven EPS line. Departure from the outside view: the US seasoned-stock 5-year distribution is NOT on file (base_rates.json us_seasoned_5y), so the card's 5-year probabilities are compared with an EST naive class in the deep-dive file (P(>=3x) ~10%, P(<=0.5x) ~12% for US mid caps [EST, unverified]); our P(>=3x) is lower on purpose (a ~10%-ROTC cyclical at 17x forward needs a re-rating and a supercycle to triple). Checked by thesis:paper-call:US-KEX:* (6 calls to 2027-09-30, plus the 3 card calls). Open soft flags: 6. P(≥3x) 0% vs base n/a; P(≤0.5x) 4% vs base n/a; EV 5-yr multiple 1.12x vs hurdle 1.47x. Review 2027-02-15.
